title: RT-DETR-R18 vs RT-DETRv2-R18: benchmark
dek: On the same COCO protocol, RT-DETRv2-R18 measures 0.9 mAP points higher than RT-DETR-R18 and runs 51.1 FPS to 47.2 on desktop GPU.
author: Vision Analysis

blocks.text: RT-DETRv2-R18 improves on RT-DETR-R18 on both axes: 50.7 vs 49.8 mAP@50-95 and 51.1 vs 47.2 FPS on an RTX 5070 Ti in PyTorch. The two share 20.18M parameters and the same peak VRAM. The v2 revision is a small gain at no measured cost.

RT-DETRv2-R18 (released 2024-05-01) is the second version; RT-DETR-R18 (2023-04-17) is the original. Both are Apache-2.0 and evaluated at 640 px with the same parameter count, so the comparison isolates what v2 changed.

blocks.caption: Accuracy vs parameters on COCO val2017. RT-DETR-R18 and RT-DETRv2-R18 highlighted against the full field.

blocks.text: mAP is shown in percent form. RT-DETRv2-R18 measures 50.7 mAP@50-95 to RT-DETR-R18's 49.8, a 0.9 point gain, and it holds a slim edge on small objects: 33.5 vs 32.7 mAP_small. The accuracy improvement is real but narrow.

In PyTorch on the RTX 5070 Ti, RT-DETRv2-R18 runs 51.1 FPS to RT-DETR-R18's 47.2, 7.68% faster. The edge carries across runtimes: 125.5 vs 120.6 FPS on TensorRT FP32, 97.1 vs 92.5 FPS on ONNX Runtime. On Jetson Orin the two are level near 10 FPS.
The verdict holds. RT-DETRv2-R18 leads on both accuracy and speed across 4 runtimes and 3 hardware platforms with verified data, from the RTX 5070 Ti to the Raspberry Pi 5.

Pick RT-DETRv2-R18 for new deployments: it is more accurate and faster than RT-DETR-R18 at the same size and memory. Pick RT-DETR-R18 only if it is already integrated and the sub-one-point accuracy gain does not justify a swap. Both are Apache-2.0.

# pip install libreyolo
from libreyolo import LibreYOLO

rtdetr = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRr18.pt")      # 20.18M params, 49.8 mAP@50-95
rtdetrv2 = LibreYOLO("LibreRTDETRv2r18.pt")  # 20.18M params, 50.7 mAP@50-95

results = rtdetrv2("image.jpg")
